title: The effects of collagen peptide supplementation on appetite and post-exercise energy intake in females: a randomised controlled trial

what_it_measured.text: This study examined whether supplementation with collagen peptides (CP) affects appetite and post-exercise energy intake in healthy active females.

dose.text: In this randomised, double-blind crossover study, fifteen healthy females (23 (SD 3) years) consumed 15 g/d of CP or a taste matched non-energy control (CON) for 7 d.

route.text: In this randomised, double-blind crossover study, fifteen healthy females (23 (SD 3) years) consumed 15 g/d of CP or a taste matched non-energy control (CON) for 7 d.

endpoint.text: We performed a sample size calculation for our primary outcome, energy intake at the ad libitum meal.

reported_results.text: Ad libitum energy intake was ~10 % (~41 kcal) lower in the CP trial (P = 0·037). There was no difference in gastrointestinal symptoms or subjective appetite sensations throughout the trial (P ≥ 0·412). Total plasma GLP-1 (AUC, CON: 6369 (SD 2330); CP: 9064 (SD 3021) pmol/l; P < 0·001) and insulin (+80 % at peak) were higher after CP (P < 0·001). Plasma ghrelin and leptin were lower in CP (condition effect; P ≤ 0·032). PYY, CCK and glucose were not different between CP and placebo (P ≥ 0·100). CP supplementation following exercise increased GLP-1 and insulin concentrations and reduced ad libitum energy intake at a subsequent meal in physically active females.
